claude.sample_unit: generated vignettes and images (10 ChatGPT regenerations per prompt per condition; MBIC image tiles)

links.outcome: Ethnoracial stereotyping in ChatGPT-generated vignettes and Bing images for genetic conditions
links.effect: Initial-prompt ChatGPT vignettes gave 100% conformity to the traditionally associated group for all five conditions; Bing images most often depicted Caucasian patients (47.4%). Self-prompting reduced conformity but gave inaccurate proportions.
links.quote: As seen in the results of this study, each of the five disorders had a 100% conformation with the single most commonly known ethnoracial identity: 100% African American for sickle cell, 100% Caucasian for cystic fibrosis, 100% Ashkenazi Jewish for Tay-Sachs disease, 100% Mediterranean for beta-thalassemia, and 100% East Asian for ALDH2 deficiency.

links.outcome: Output variability across repeated runs, prompt changes, and time (March vs May 2024)
links.effect: Change in historically associated group share over time was significant (t(9)=2.63, p=0.027); between initial and self-prompts also significant (t(9)=2.80, p=0.021).
links.quote: Change over months, between March and May, was statistically significant ( t (9) = 2.63, p = 0.027) (Table 1 ).

links.outcome: Change in depicted ethnoracial identity of patients with prompt modification
links.effect: Self-prompting shifted historically associated group share from 100% to 25% (sickle cell), 20% (CF), 15% (Tay-Sachs), 0% (beta-thalassemia), 90% (ALDH2); Bing secondary prompting raised sickle cell African depiction from 25% to 100%.
links.quote: For change over prompts, between IP and SP, a paired t -test was statistically significant ( t (9) = 2.80, p = 0.021) (Table 2 ).

unlisted_practices: Prompt engineering (specifying context and requiring epidemiologically aligned diverse demographics) to reduce stereotyped demographics in AI-generated educational vignettes

links.outcome: Ethnoracial stereotypes in generated educational vignettes
links.effect: Initial vignettes had 100% conformation: African American/sickle cell, Caucasian/cystic fibrosis, Ashkenazi Jewish/Tay-Sachs, Mediterranean/beta-thalassemia, and East Asian/ALDH2.
links.quote: As seen in the results of this study, each of the five disorders had a 100% conformation with the single most commonly known ethnoracial identity: 100% African American for sickle cell, 100% Caucasian for cystic fibrosis, 100% Ashkenazi Jewish for Tay-Sachs disease, 100% Mediterranean for beta-thalassemia, and 100% East Asian for ALDH2 deficiency.

links.effect: Generated ALDH2 cases were 95% East Asian versus 26.6% frequency among East Asians for the most prevalent variant.
links.quote: Cases of ALDH2 were 95% East Asian descent, which deviates from records showing the most prevalent ALDH2 variant to have a frequency of 26.6% among East Asians, which is ten (10) times higher than the next most common variants found in other ethnoracial groups [ 27 ].

unlisted_practices: Prompt engineering/self-prompting with epidemiology-incidence prompts to diversify ethnoracial representation in AI-generated medical education cases.
